desc:
Return true if the integer n can be written as 2k for some integer k ≥ 0, and false otherwise.

Zero and negative numbers are never powers of two. Try to answer without loops or recursion.

n = 16  →  true
n = 12  →  false
hints: Look at the binary form of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. What do they all have in common?
A power of two has exactly one bit set. What does subtracting 1 do to such a number?
For n > 0, n - 1 flips the single 1 bit to 0 and turns every lower bit into 1, so n & (n - 1) is 0 exactly when n is a power of two.
editorial: A positive power of two has a single 1 bit, for example 1000. Subtracting one gives 0111, which shares no bit with the original, so n & (n - 1) == 0. For any other positive number the highest set bit survives the subtraction, so the AND is not zero.

Remember to reject n ≤ 0 first: 0 & -1 is also zero, and negative numbers in two's complement have many bits set. The check takes constant time. Alternatives such as repeated halving or testing n & -n == n also work.
